message.content:
<?php
$stdin = fopen('php://stdin', 'r');
$inputString = stream_get_contents($stdin);
fclose($stdin);
$inputString = trim($inputString);
$inputLines = array_map('trim', explode("\n", $inputString));
$currentLine = 0;

function readLine() {
    global $inputLines, $currentLine;
    return $inputLines[$currentLine++];
}

$word = readLine();
if (strpos($word, 'H') !== false || strpos($word, 'Q') !== false || strpos($word, '9') !== false) {
    echo "YES\n";
} else {
    echo "NO\n";
}
?>

<?php
$input = file_get_contents('php://stdin');
$lines = array_map('trim', explode("\n", trim($input)));
$word = $lines[0] ?? '';

if (strpos($word, 'H') !== false || strpos($word, 'Q') !== false || strpos($word, '9') !== false) {
    echo "YES\n";
} else {
    echo "NO\n";
}
message.reasoning_content:
The user wants a translation of Node.js code to PHP. The Node.js code reads from stdin, processes input lines, and checks if a string contains 'H', 'Q', or '9'.

Key differences:
- Node.js uses event-based stdin reading. PHP typically reads all stdin at once using `fopen('php://stdin', 'r')` or `file_get_contents('php://stdin')`.
- The `readLine` function in Node.js uses a global array and index. In PHP, we can just read all lines into an array and use an index or array_shift.
- `console.log` becomes `echo` or `print`.
- `string.includes` becomes `strpos !== false` or `str_contains` (PHP 8+). I'll use `strpos` for broader compatibility or `str_contains` if assuming modern PHP. Since no version specified, `strpos` is safer.

Plan:
1. Read all input from stdin.
2. Split by newlines, trim each line.
3. Get the first line (word).
4. Check for characters.
5. Output YES/NO.

source_data.prob_desc_description: HQ9+ is a joke programming language which has only four one-character instructions: "H" prints "Hello, World!", "Q" prints the source code of the program itself, "9" prints the lyrics of "99 Bottles of Beer" song,  "+" increments the value stored in the internal accumulator.Instructions "H" and "Q" are case-sensitive and must be uppercase. The characters of the program which are not instructions are ignored.You are given a program written in HQ9+. You have to figure out whether executing this program will produce any output.
source_data.prob_desc_output_spec: Output "YES", if executing the program will produce any output, and "NO" otherwise.
source_data.prob_desc_input_spec: The input will consist of a single line p which will give a program in HQ9+. String p will contain between 1 and 100 characters, inclusive. ASCII-code of each character of p will be between 33 (exclamation mark) and 126 (tilde), inclusive.
source_data.prob_desc_notes: NoteIn the first case the program contains only one instruction — "H", which prints "Hello, World!".In the second case none of the program characters are language instructions.
